title: Coskeleta of truncated simplicial objects as finite limits, and their preservation
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits] and let $m\geq0$. Let $\Delta$ be the category of the ordered sets $[k]=\{0<\dots<k\}$ and order-preserving maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n\geq0$ let $(\Delta/[n])_{\leq m}$ be the finite category whose objects are the morphisms $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ of $\Delta$ with $k\leq m$ and whose morphisms $(\alpha':[k']\to[n])\to(\alpha:[k]\to[n])$ are the morphisms $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ of $\Delta$ with $\alpha\circ\psi=\alpha'$. For an $m$-truncated simplicial object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] let $U(n):(\Delta/[n])_{\leq m}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ be the functor $(\alpha:[k]\to[n])\mapsto U_k$, $\psi\mapsto U(\psi)$. Then: (1) the $m$-coskeleton $\operatorname{cosk}_mU$ of $U$ exists in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]; one may take $(\operatorname{cosk}_mU)_n=\lim U(n)$, with $\operatorname{cosk}_mU(\varphi)$ for $\varphi:[n]\to[n']$ the morphism of limits induced by $\alpha\mapsto\varphi\circ\alpha$, and the counit $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_m\operatorname{cosk}_mU\to U$ is an isomorphism; (2) if $\mathcal D$ is a category and $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is a functor preserving finite limits, then the simplicial object $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_mU$ of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] together with $\Phi(\varepsilon)$ is an $m$-coskeleton of the $m$-truncated simplicial object $\Phi\circ U$; consequently, if $K$ is a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ whose canonical morphism $K\to\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_mK$ is an isomorphism, then $\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_m(\Phi\circ K)$ exists and the canonical morphism $\Phi\circ K\to\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_m(\Phi\circ K)$ is an isomorphism; (3) for a morphism $\beta:U\to U'$ of $m$-truncated simplicial objects of $\mathcal C$ there is a unique morphism $\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta:\operatorname{cosk}_mU\to\operatorname{cosk}_mU'$ with $\varepsilon'\circ\mathrm{sk}_m(\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta)=\beta\circ\varepsilon$; this is functorial, so $\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta$ is an isomorphism when $\beta$ is, and when $\Phi$ is as in (2), $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta=\operatorname{cosk}_m(\Phi\circ\beta)$ for the coskeleta of (2); (4) in particular, for a category $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal C=\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal E)$ the category of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal E$ (which has finite limits, computed objectwise), every evaluation functor $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(V)$, $V$ an object of $\mathcal E$, preserves finite limits, so (2) and (3) apply to it, with $\mathcal D$ the category of sets.
